newsitem.title: ITALY: BASKETBALL-OLYMPIAKOS LIFT EUROPEAN TITLE AT LAST.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-OLYMPIAKOS LIFT EUROPEAN TITLE AT LAST.

text.p: Olympiakos made it third time lucky when they won the European club basketball championship on Thursday, beating Barcelona 73-58 in the final.
The Greek side, losing finalists in 1994 and 1995, controlled much of the second half and deserved their victory, the most famous in their history.
But it was more sadness for Barcelona, beaten finalists in 1996 and now without anything to show from six Final Four appearances in the last nine years.
Olympiakos, inspired as they had been in Tuesday's semifinals against Ljubljana by ex-Los Angeles Lakers playmaker David Rivers, overcame a slow start to thoroughly earn the crown.
After seven minutes Olympiakos only had two points on the board but with Rivers in top form, scoring 14 in the first half alone, they went into the break with a 31-29 advantage.

In the second half it took Barcelona four minutes to add to their halftime tally as they slipped to 38-29 and when Olympiakos stretched into a double figure lead at 44-33, courtesy of some Rivers magic, it was fairly clear where the title was bound.
Rivers led the scoring with 26 to go with the magnificentt 28 he scored in the semifinal.
The event has been a tour de force for the 30-year-old and as he held the trophy afterwards he was lifted aloft by his team mates.
Dragan Tarlac, steady with his freethrows, contributed a valuable 11 points to ensure Olympiakos fans and much of Greece could go off and celebrate in style.
The fans stayed long to savour the great moment. They had more than half-filled the 12,000 seater-stadium and made their presence felt every minute of the tournament.
Police in riot gear surrounded the playing court after the match but were not needed.
It was a disappointing night for Barcelona and their 2,000 followers, mindful of the final 12 months ago when they lost by just one point to Panathinaikos in highly controversial circumstances.

On Thursday, there could be no argument. Serbian guard Sasha Djordjevic, so influential in Tuesday's victory over Villeurbanne of France, played a big role in the first half as he and Rivers duelled for supremacy.
But he was less effective in the second and ended the night with just six points.
